qualifying_findings.title: GitHub Copilot coding agent can now use custom MCP servers in Visual Studio Code
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: GitHub says Copilot coding agent in Visual Studio Code can use custom MCP servers, letting teams connect agent workflows to external services and internal developer systems through configured MCP endpoints.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: MCP access is moving into day-to-day coding-agent execution, so local practice should treat MCP server selection, credential custody, tool-scope review, workspace policy, and approval evidence as part of IDE coding-agent governance rather than as optional integration detail.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Route broad Copilot, VS Code, and MCP product/protocol coverage upstream; retain local synthesis around governed custom-server use inside coding-agent workflows.

qualifying_findings.title: GitHub Copilot code review custom instructions are generally available
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: GitHub says custom instructions for Copilot code review are generally available, allowing organizations and repositories to steer review behavior with persisted guidance.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: AI review quality increasingly depends on durable review rubrics encoded near the source. Local coding-practice guidance should distinguish repository-level review instructions, organization-wide norms, and generated-review evidence from one-off reviewer prompts.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Consider whether local intelligent-code-review and code-review-evals leaves should record custom-instruction maintenance as a review-governance practice.

qualifying_findings.title: GitHub Copilot deprecates custom code guidelines in favor of repository instructions
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: GitHub says Copilot custom code guidelines are deprecated and directs users toward repository custom instructions and related instruction-file mechanisms for future guidance.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Provider-specific guidance surfaces can churn. Local instruction architecture should keep durable team norms in portable repository artifacts where possible, track provider mappings separately, and avoid treating a single product's guideline UI as the authoritative source of development standards.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Use as evidence for portable instruction-file strategy; product migration details belong upstream.

qualifying_findings.title: OpenAI Codex CLI changelog adds runtime and workflow controls
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: OpenAI's Codex changelog lists Codex CLI updates on August 27, 2026, including changes around local runtime behavior and developer workflow control surfaces.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Coding-agent runtime surfaces change quickly, so local harness and source-workflow guidance should preserve the distinction between stable operating policies and provider-specific CLI flags, defaults, and session behavior.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: A future ingest pass should cite only the specific runtime-control implication that maps to local pages; broad Codex release history remains upstream-owned.

qualifying_findings.title: Harness explains agent-ready repository structure for AI code review
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: Harness describes an agent-ready repository as one with clear ownership metadata, review boundaries, tests, documentation, and signals that help AI code-review agents locate context and produce actionable feedback.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The post supports the local idea that AI code review is a repository-information architecture problem. Review agents need source ownership, test intent, conventions, and retrieval hints, not just model access at pull-request time.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Use as practice evidence for repository readiness and review context; avoid duplicating Harness product coverage locally.

qualifying_findings.title: Semgrep advises using AI carefully in security code review
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: Semgrep discusses where AI can assist security code review and where deterministic rules, reviewer judgment, and validation remain necessary. The guidance emphasizes augmenting security review instead of delegating final assurance to generated comments.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This is local evidence for layered AI review roles: AI review should triage, explain, and route likely findings while deterministic checks and human security review remain acceptance gates for high-risk changes.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Potential local synthesis should connect security review roles to verification gates and regression repair, not create a local Semgrep product page.
